quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai half-year report: 2026 Half-Year Report (08-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 financial detail (half-year report): operating cost RMB 1,872,682,598.96, up 17.99% against revenue up 32.92%; R&D expense RMB 208,843,303.94, up 29.89%; operating cash flow RMB -1,113,134,302.58, which the company attributes to higher raw-material purchasing; exchange loss about RMB 2.02 hundred million. Prepayments rose 230.78% to RMB 557,830,256.43, inventory 34.57% to RMB 3,197,101,475.74 (mainly raw materials) and construction in progress 107.03% to RMB 947,472,423.38 (mainly equipment purchases). The US subsidiary Cambridge Industries USA (R&D and trading) had H1 revenue of RMB 233,958.63 ten-thousand and net profit of RMB 61,973.10 ten-thousand; Zhejiang Cambridge (manufacturing) had revenue of RMB 133,811.70 ten-thousand and a net loss of RMB -16,142.75 ten-thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D RMB 208,843,303.94 (+29.89%); operating cash flow RMB -1,113,134,302.58; construction in progress RMB 947,472,423.38

quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai half-year report: 2026 Half-Year Report (08-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Optical modules (half-year report): new-generation 1.6T OSFP 2xDR4 and 1.6T OSFP 2xFR4 modules, based on two 3nm DSP chips and 200G/lane high-density silicon photonics from several vendors, completed certification testing, with large-volume shipments expected in H2 2026; the high-power external light source module ELSFP completed development validation and customer sampling, with volume shipments expected to start in H2 2026. New-generation silicon-photonics 800G OSFP 2xFR4/2xLR4 and 800G 2xDR4/2xDR4+ modules passed certification at several large overseas customers and shipped in large volumes in H1 2026, with capacity to expand further in H2. New projects started in H1 2026 - 1.6T 2xDR4 LRO, 1.6T 2xLR4 10km, a 12.8T XPO and customised 3.2T, 6.4T and 7.2T NPO products for several customers - are expected to go through validation and customer sampling in H2 2026. The company says progress on 1.6T modules, ELSFP modules and NPO with several customers exceeded expectations.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T OSFP 2xDR4 / 2xFR4 large-volume shipments expected H2 2026; ELSFP volume shipments from H2 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai half-year report: 2026 Half-Year Report (08-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capacity (half-year report): the Jiashan No. 2 optoelectronic factory opened in March 2026, completed its full move-in in H1 and is expanding step by step, with 800G OSFP 2xDR4/2xDR4+, 800G OSFP 2xFR4/2xLR4 and 1.6T OSFP 2xDR4/2xDR4+ capacity scaled up at Jiashan No. 2 and the overseas factory for 2026-2027 orders. The Malaysia base completed its phase-2 workshop expansion, building a complete overseas end-to-end module manufacturing system; a phase-3 building is due to start production in H2 2026 with a large capacity increase; the base is advancing 1.6T production and its yield rose more than 15% year on year. In Mexico, broadband trial production finished in H1 2026, and the optical-module cleanroom factory is designed, with construction completion and production start expected in early 2027; the Massachusetts (US) factory is being reconfigured to start trial production of next-generation wireless routers and broadband products from H1 2027; Vietnam base lines passed customer audits.
quarterly_data.figure: Malaysia phase-3 production H2 2026; Mexico module factory production early 2027; Malaysia yield up more than 15%

quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai half-year report: 2026 Half-Year Report (08-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain (half-year report): North American demand for 800G and 1.6T modules and next-generation optical connectivity keeps growing fast while core-material supply pressure keeps rising; the company secures key materials through investment, fixed-asset spending and prepayments, strengthens qualification and delivery management of core suppliers of DSP chips, silicon-photonics chips, CW lasers, Faraday rotators / isolators and fiber components (MT-FA, AWG), and ordered several key materials early to lock capacity for large-volume delivery in H2 2026 and 2027. In broadband and wireless, memory (DDR, Flash), PCB and MLCC prices rose sharply: memory's share of a Wi-Fi product's bill of materials rose from under 10% at the start of the year to about 40%, and H1 broadband and wireless shipments and revenue fell year on year; the company expects continued material price rises and longer lead times to suppress end demand from H2 2026 into 2027 and squeeze its product margins.
quarterly_data.figure: memory share of Wi-Fi bill of materials from under 10% to about 40%

quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai half-year report: 2026 Half-Year Report (08-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Broadband and wireless (half-year report): 25G PON, XGS PON and 10G EPON were over 60% of H1 2026 broadband shipments and revenue; the company won new projects from a major European operator and a major US operator for volume shipment in 2027, and an AI-engine PON gateway is to ship in small batches in H2 2026. Wi-Fi 7 was over 60% of wireless shipments; four carrier-grade Wi-Fi 8 home gateways were launched as projects, with volume shipments expected in early 2027; the AIU-100 AI edge embedded server (over 200 TOPS) has been sampled to industry customers.
quarterly_data.figure: Wi-Fi 8 gateway volume shipments expected early 2027; operator projects ship in 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: CIG Shanghai half-year report: 2026 Half-Year Report (08-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: H2 2026 plan (half-year report, company plan with a forward-looking-statement caveat): speed up line expansion at the Jiashan and Malaysia factories and construction of the Mexico factory, striving to reach the planned expansion targets by year-end to secure North American core-customer orders; strive to complete core-customer test certification and mass production of optical modules within the year; push 1.6T series and LPO / LRO low-power products through development, mass production and customer certification, and promote ELSFP, XPO and NPO. The company notes that capacity plans and mass-production timing may be affected by the industry cycle, technology iteration and trade policy.
